question: Can ExaCA's own (deterministic) GoogleTest unit tests be used as upstream validation evidence for this build?
answer: They were built and run: 30 of 52 passed under CTest. Attribution (same day, see the matrix file) showed 0 application-class failures: 7 TEST_FIXTURE (host/device view handling in unit_test/*.hpp; all pass after a fixture-only patch), 13 UNSUPPORTED_CONFIG (host-space test variants inside a CUDA-enabled build; all pass in a Serial-only build), 2 TEST_INFRA (CTest runs mpiexec without per-rank GPU binding; both pass through the project launcher). Upstream's own small full-application cases pass at 1/2/4 real GPUs within upstream tolerances. Unmodified tests under CTest's own launcher still fail in this environment.

how_built.gtest: GoogleTest is not installed in this environment; the artifact carries Kokkos' vendored fused GoogleTest 1.11.0 at deps/kokkos/tpls/gtest (LICENSE + README + gtest.h + gtest-all.cc). It was compiled into a static library in the private build tree and exposed through GTEST_ROOT: a build-side shim, no source change, no system installation, the artifact and the validated benchmark install are untouched.
how_built.configure: cmake -S src -B build/level3/exaca/cuda-unittests -DExaCA_ENABLE_TESTING=ON -DExaCA_REQUIRE_EXTERNAL_JSON=ON -DExaCA_REQUIRE_FINCH=OFF with the benchmark's Kokkos 4.7.04 and nlohmann_json prefixes
how_built.install_required: cmake --install is required before running: the tests resolve material/orientation files by bare name through ExaCA_DATA_INSTALL (<prefix>/share/ExaCA); without it 6 tests fail with 'Could not locate/open .../Inconel625.json'

result.deterministic: two consecutive ctest runs produced an identical pass/fail pattern

inspected_causes.class: invalid test configuration in a device build
inspected_causes.evidence: the host-space ('SERIAL') test variants abort with 'Kokkos::View ERROR: attempt to access inaccessible memory space' followed by cudaErrorAssert; the harness generates host and device variants for every enabled backend, but in a CUDA-enabled build Kokkos' default execution space is Cuda, so application kernels touch host-space views
inspected_causes.conclusion: inconclusive here; a Serial-only build would be needed to run these variants meaningfully

inspected_causes.evidence: tstOrientation.hpp:108 compares against a view obtained with Kokkos::create_mirror_view WITHOUT a copy, so it reads uninitialised host memory (observed values are recycled text bytes); tstInterface aborts with 'Kokkos::View ERROR: attempt to access inaccessible memory space (label="DOCenter")', a host access to a device view
inspected_causes.conclusion: test-side issues exposed by Kokkos 4.7's access checks; they do not demonstrate a defect in the application kernels

inspected_causes.evidence: tstNucleation.hpp:311/313/315 (grain_id of the three cells that must not nucleate) fail on the CUDA variants at every rank count; ExaCA_Update_test_CUDA np_2/np_4 abort without a gtest assertion
inspected_causes.conclusion: not explained; must be investigated before any claim in either direction

consequences: the ExaCA acceptance continues to rest only on the project-defined statistical protocol (references/validation_protocol.md), which covers the dirsolid smoke case at 1/2/4 GPUs and nothing else
no upstream unit test result is counted as PASS anywhere in this repository
follow-up (not done): a Serial-only test build for the host variants, an upstream report for the mirror-view issues, and an explanation of the Nucleation/Update CUDA failures
artifacts_local_only: build/level3/exaca/cuda-unittests (build tree), /tmp scratch logs of the two ctest runs; not committed
superseded_by: references/upstream_unit_test_matrix.json (per-test matrix, classifications, retests) -- this file keeps the first observation of 2026-09-11
correction: An earlier statement in this repository said upstream had no full-application numerical reference. That was wrong: unit_test/tstUpdate.hpp checks VolFractionNucleated against 0.1882 +- 0.0100 for Inp_SmallDirSolidification.json and TimeStepOfOutput against 4820 +- 1 for Inp_SmallEquiaxedGrain.json. Those references apply to those two SMALL official cases only; they are not transferable to this benchmark's 128^3 dirsolid case and do not relax its frozen statistical protocol.
